title: 🏛️ Exams 2002–2025 · comparative or superlative: read the clue ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, general) A text about children and chores says: "... children are capable of handling (much / more / most) than we may believe." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "than": the comparative is used to compare two things, here what children can handle and what we believe. "Most" is a superlative and does not go with "than", and "much" and "many" are quantity words that cannot stand alone as the comparative here.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) A text about cycling says: "While cars pollute the environment, bikes are petrol-free. They are ___ to run, buy and fix than cars." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "than cars": two things are compared, and "cheap" is a short adjective, so it takes -er: cheaper. "Cheapest" is the superlative of a group, "cheap" does not compare anything, and "more cheap" uses "more" with a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2017, general) A text weighs the good points of eating cocoa and dark chocolate: "The ___ value in eating cocoa and dark chocolate may be their ability to lower blood pressure." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "the" in front of the blank and a group of values: the value that stands at the top of all of them takes the superlative of a short adjective, the + -est. The consonant doubles: big, biggest. "Bigger" compares only two things, "big" compares nothing, and "most big" uses "most" with a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) A text about shopping says: "Using the Internet can be (funnier / fun / funniest) and a convenient way of shopping and finding out information." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared in this sentence: there is no "than", no "as ... as" and no group of three things. So the plain word is needed: it can be fun and a convenient way of shopping. "Funnier" would need "than", and "funniest" and "most fun" would need "the" and a group.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) A text about tigers says: "They are ___ wonderful to watch in nature than in the zoo." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "than": two places are compared, nature and the zoo. "Wonderful" is a long adjective, so it takes "more" in front of it. "Most" is a superlative, "faster" is already a comparative and cannot stand in front of another adjective, and "much" cannot replace "more" before an adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) A text on household chores explains: "When children help out, chores get done sooner, and parents have (more / less / least) to do." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is the meaning: when the children help, the chores get done sooner, so the parents have a smaller amount to do: less. "More" says the opposite. "Least" is a superlative: it would need a group of people to be compared with, and "much" does not compare anything.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2008) A mother has given up a bad habit. She feels healthier and she saves money, then she adds: "But ___ important thing is that I want to be around for my kids for as long as possible." Which words complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: The mother puts her kids above everything else, so the thing is at the top of all the reasons: the superlative "the most" with a long adjective. "The more" compares only two things, "the least" is a superlative too but it would make the wish to be around for her kids the smallest of her concerns, which the sentence denies, and "most" forgets "the".
